# ACMElabs design system

This repository owns the Lit components with the acme- prefix and their shared delivery, React bridge and consumer tools. One workflow serves all five packages. Current work belongs to [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md).

## Session start

From a package directory, find the Git repository root and use it for this workflow. Complete these steps before starting the requested work.

1. Read [status](docs/STATUS.md), [domain routing](docs/agents/domain.md), [the context map](CONTEXT-MAP.md) and the glossary for the task. Read each selected file to its last line.
2. Read [the specification index](spec/README.md), then the active specification, plan and task list named by status. Read [the record layout](docs/agents/workflow.md). Preserve an incomplete plan when Peter changes the request.
3. Inspect Git status and the active branch. Verify the selected Bun executable and its version. Preserve work owned by other sessions. Read [repository ownership](docs/agents/repository.md) and [verification](docs/agents/verification.md) before editing; identify authored inputs, generated outputs, affected packages and applicable check evidence.
4. Establish the baseline from its revision, inputs and check scope. Run missing or invalidated checks using the verification guide. A historical green result does not close a newer failure.
5. Report the phase, last completed step, next step, red checks and pending decisions in five lines or fewer. Follow Peter's current request. A request to continue resumes the next approved task; a completed plan does not authorize another feature.

## Work through brain

Use brain:using-brain to select the applicable skill. Agent-skills remains available. When both plugins provide the same skill, use brain's version. The plugins own the lifecycle and engineering procedures; this repository supplies its facts and record locations.

A user-owned decision or permission uses brain:ask-user-question and its host reference. Keep approval scoped to the actual task and action. The status file records current authorization; a completed pass or another repository grants no standing permission here.

Setup, wait-what, handoff, triage and wayfinder start from Peter's prompt. When one is needed, give him the applicable command or skill invocation. [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) carries Claude command spellings; Codex uses the installed skill names.

Before changing an area, read the applicable decisions and research through their [decision](docs/decisions/README.md) and [research](docs/research/README.md) indexes. Use the glossary's names. Source facts, proposals, selected contracts and verification results remain distinct.

| Change | Required guidance |
| --- | --- |
| Component behavior or interface | [Component rules](docs/development/components.md), [interface conventions](docs/development/interfaces.md), and its owning specification |
| CSS or style production | [Style ownership](docs/development/styles.md); [generation and comparison](docs/development/generation.md) when mapped sources or census evidence change |
| Package or dependency responsibility | [Selected stack](docs/development/stack.md) and the package ownership map |
| Website, examples or consumer guidance | [Documentation rules](docs/development/documentation.md) |
| A reference comparison | [Reference sources](docs/development/reference-sources.md) |
| A domain term or decision record | brain:domain-modeling and [domain routing](docs/agents/domain.md) |
| A skill or agent instruction file | The official skill-creator workflow and brain:writing-for-agents |

## Task end and handoff

1. Update the task's acceptance checks and any specification whose facts change. Record research or a decision in its one owning record.
2. Save exact verification commands, results, revision and limits. Use focused checks for each slice, then the full gate and review at the task's closure.
3. Rewrite [status](docs/STATUS.md) with the next action, anything red and what awaits Peter. Include the exact invocation when the next step is user-started. A fresh session must resume without the conversation.
4. Record what is committed, uncommitted, pushed or awaiting approval. Stage owned files by name. Use only the local-commit and outward-action authorization actually granted for this work. Merge approved pull requests with merge commits.

Historical plans and releases provide evidence. They do not restart their completed phases. The [local issue tracker](docs/agents/issue-tracker.md) owns unresolved follow-ups; its [labels](docs/agents/triage-labels.md) define their status.

@AGENTS.md

## Claude Code

The imported project rules are shared with other coding agents. Both workflow plugins are enabled in the project settings.

| Phase | Claude command |
| --- | --- |
| Specification | /brain:spec |
| Planning | /brain:plan |
| Implementation | /brain:build, or /brain:build auto within an approved plan |
| Diagnosis and verification | /brain:test |
| Review | /brain:review |
| Shipping | /brain:ship |

The shared instructions define the user-started boundary. Its Claude commands are /brain:setup-brain, /brain:wait-what, /brain:handoff, /brain:triage and /brain:wayfinder.

Project settings name the addy-agent-skills and acmelabs marketplaces. Installed plugin versions come from the host, not a cached version in this file.

# Task 9 root and shared workflow review

Verdict: **ACCEPTED after two narrow corrections**. No required finding remains.

This is an independent document review of inactive root drafts and shared workflow records. It does not establish actual Claude or Codex startup behavior. Task 11 still owns activation; task 12 owns clean-candidate and host-session acceptance.

## Findings and correction review

| ID | Initial finding and evidence | Verified correction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1 | The original AGENTS draft step 3 inspected Git state but did not require inspecting the selected runtime. The approved specification explicitly requires both Git state and the pinned runtime at `spec/SPEC-maintainer-workflow.md:183`. Reading the verification guide establishes the requirement; it does not establish which executable the host selects. | `.artifacts/AGENTS.next.md:11` now requires verification of the selected Bun executable and its version before work. The runtime policy stays in the verification guide; no second version inventory is added. Resolved. |
| R2 | Original `.artifacts/CLAUDE.next.md:7` and `:20` repeated the shared brain-precedence, question, glossary and instruction-authoring rules already owned by AGENTS. The specification requires a host-specific remainder after the import (`SPEC-maintainer-workflow.md:58–62,68–72`). Task 9 also requires one owner per rule (`tasks/todo.md:182–184`). Brain's writing-for-agents guidance makes the same distinction. | Both shared-rule paragraphs are removed. The 18-line CLAUDE draft starts with `@AGENTS.md`, lists Claude command spellings and records Claude project-plugin setup. Its user-started command list points to the shared boundary instead of redefining it. Resolved. |

The coordinator made these changes. I re-read the changed startup section and the complete corrected CLAUDE draft. No implementation file changed during this review.

## Contract coverage and limits

**Complete reads.** I read all three root draft files, the four assigned agent guides, all five maintenance issue files, CONTEXT-MAP.md and the full approved workflow specification and plan. I also read the task 9/11/12 acceptance sections in todo.md, including checkpoint C/D requirements. The full current AGENTS, CLAUDE and project settings from both reference projects were read. Installed source reads covered using-brain, using-agent-skills, writing-for-agents, brain's phase-boundary reference, and its local tracker, triage-label and domain templates.

**Startup and resumption.** AGENTS lines 7–13 route package starts to the root, require complete selected reads, preserve other sessions' work, inspect actual Git/runtime state, validate the baseline and limit continuation to an approved task. Lines 37–40 require task acceptance, exact verification evidence and a current status that supports a fresh session without conversation history. The workflow guide preserves an incomplete plan when the request changes and keeps one active status/plan pair. These rules provide the durable state needed after interruption or compaction. Brain owns the choice of phase boundary and compact/handoff procedure; the root does not create a second process. Actual interruption/compaction behavior remains a host-evaluation question, not a document-review pass.

**Approval and authority.** AGENTS lines 17–21 select brain when skill names overlap and delegate user-owned choices to brain's question skill and host reference. Approval remains scoped to the actual task/action. Lines 13 and 40 prevent a completed plan or another repository from granting new work or outward-action permission. The two reference projects' different standing commit/push grants are not copied. The five user-started boundaries remain explicit. Setup guidance is used as a template; no setup command or global hook is invoked.

**Shared packages and domains.** AGENTS line 3 and workflow lines 26–32 establish one workflow for all five packages. Tasks identify inputs, generated outputs, affected packages and checks before editing. Domain lines 3–9 and CONTEXT-MAP lines 5–10 keep the existing component and tooling contexts. Shared component terms have one glossary owner. No package-per-glossary expansion, new product vocabulary or duplicated decision store is introduced. Current requirements, source observations, selected decisions and historical verification remain distinct.

**Record adapters.** The workflow guide maps intent/interview outputs to docs/design while retaining the installed procedure. Status, current plans, completed plans, decisions, research, evidence, live verification and scratch output have separate owners.
